2.text: their leisure time with athletic exercise, wrestling, running, fencing with spears,

3.text: etc. They were more ready for war, which was more frequent than it is now.

4.text: In war the family-group acted as a unit against all other parties.

5.text: The Russian officials of the Kolyma country, when endeavoring to bring

6.text: the Chukchee under Russian allegiance, treated them in the same way as the

7.text: Yakut and the Tungus of eastern Siberia. These tribes had strictly organized

8.text: clans (родъ, pl. роды), which could not intermingle as readily as the Chukchee
8.note: Pre-reform Cyrillic (родъ with word-final hard sign ъ after a consonant, роды plural without it) — §2.7, keyed as printed. Machine text had garbled Latin substitutes.

9.text: vaˊrat. The Cossacks and their chiefs, when subjugating these tribes, taxed
9.note: Raised mark keyed as stress U+02CA per §2.1/§4 default, never apostrophe. Compound yaˊnřa-vaˊrat is ratified in the lexicon (2-008, 2-049) though standalone vaˊrat has no key of its own.

10.text: each clan separately. Therefore Russian officials, when trying to levy tribute

11.text: on the Chukchee, invented clans and even clan-chiefs.¹ Baron von Maydell,
11.note: Footnote body marker keyed as superscript U+00B9, not the ASCII '!' the machine text substituted — §2.10.

12.text: who was the chief official of the Kolyma district in 1868-70, even invented

13.text: a new rank and title, “The Highest Chief of all the Chukchee.” This sounds
13.note: Closing quote keyed curly U+201D per §1/§5.6; machine text had straight/escaped.

14.text: almost royal; and, indeed, the Russians sometimes called the person having

15.text: this rank “Chukchee King,” “Black King of the Tundra,” “Chukchee Czar.”
15.note: Closing quote keyed curly U+201D per §1/§5.6.

16.text: All this was quite imaginary. The family that was given this title was simply

17.text: a rich reindeer-breeding family with some influence among its neighbors. I

18.text: lived with this family for a few months, and shall speak of it later on in

19.note: Footnote body marker keyed as superscript U+00B2, not the ASCII '?' the machine text substituted — §2.10.

20.text: The clans introduced by the Russians were also invented, and had no

21.text: standing in the aboriginal organization of the tribe. The whole territory of

22.text: the Chukchee was divided into five parts; and each of these parts, with the

23.text: people living in it, was called a “clan.” Some rich reindeer-breeder among
23.note: Closing quote keyed curly U+201D per §1/§5.6.

24.text: those friendly disposed to the Russians was called “chief,” and that was all.

25.text: The Chukchee living beyond the sphere of influence of the Russian officials

26.text: in the tundra to the west of the Chaun River and on the Chukchee Peninsula,

27.text: reindeer-breeders and maritime hunters, were called “the maritime clan.” Even
27.note: Closing quote keyed curly U+201D per §1/§5.6.

28.text: the tribute was nominal, — 247 rubles from all the clans, — though the
28.note: Comma before each em dash per the printed page (not a period); dashes are em U+2014 per §2.11.

29.text: Chukchee tribe has several thousand adult men. This tribute is paid in the

30.text: following way. In the parts of the territory nearest to the Russian settlements,

31.text: at least every other family pays a tribute of one ruble. It is understood that

32.text: this sum represents the tribute of one man, as among the Tungus and the

33.text: Yakut;³ but, as I have said, it is not true. The tribute is paid by a family;
33.note: Footnote body marker keyed as superscript U+00B3, tight against the semicolon, not the ASCII '8' the machine text substituted — §2.10.

34.text: and not all the families pay, either. Those that are unfriendly to the Russians

35.note: Footnote opener marker keyed as superscript U+00B9 with following space, per §2.10.

36.text: authorities. Each community has a man who is richer than the others, or who has a larger family; but he

37.text: also is little obeyed and has no right to punish anybody” (Sarytcheff, Journey in the Northeastern Part of Sibe-

40.text: ³ Maydell also tried to introduce among the Reindeer Chukchee a tribute of half a ruble from a boy under
40.note: Footnote opener marker keyed as superscript U+00B3 with following space, per §2.10.

41.text: sixteen years, but this attempt was not successful. So the tribute which at first was settled as 316 rubles was

42.text: lowered to 247 rubles. At the same time Maydell tried to take a census of the Reindeer Chukchee. The

43.text: figures of his census are 476 men and 369 women; total 845. He is quite well aware, however, of the defi-

44.text: ciencies of this census. He does not even give these figures in his book. I borrowed them from the documents
